title: RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
subtitle: Core Argument Coverage Plan: Hybrid Parametric/Non-Parametric Memory

nodes.title: Problem: Limitations of Purely Parametric Models
nodes.purpose: Define the research gap: large pre-trained models store knowledge but lack precise access, updatability, and provenance, leading to hallucinations on knowledge-intensive tasks.

nodes.title: Method: RAG Architecture Overview
nodes.purpose: Explain the core mechanism combining a pre-trained seq2seq generator (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index (DPR) as non-parametric memory, trained end-to-end.

nodes.title: Formalism: RAG-Sequence vs. RAG-Token Marginalization
nodes.purpose: Detail the mathematical distinction between the two formulations: marginalizing over documents per sequence vs. per token, including the latent variable treatment.

nodes.title: Procedure: Training Objective and Decoding Strategies
nodes.purpose: Describe the negative marginal log-likelihood training objective, the decision to freeze the document encoder, and the 'Thorough' vs. 'Fast' decoding approximations.

nodes.title: Result: State-of-the-Art Open-Domain QA
nodes.purpose: Present evidence that RAG outperforms closed-book (T5) and extractive open-book (DPR, REALM) models on NQ, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, and CuratedTrec without specialized pre-training.

nodes.title: Result: Factual and Specific Language Generation
nodes.purpose: Demonstrate RAG's superiority in abstractive QA (MS-MARCO) and Jeopardy question generation regarding factuality, specificity, and diversity compared to BART baselines.

nodes.title: Result: Fact Verification without Retrieval Supervision
nodes.purpose: Show that RAG achieves competitive accuracy on FEVER classification tasks despite lacking gold evidence supervision during training, unlike pipeline SOTA models.

nodes.title: Analysis: Importance of Learned Retrieval
nodes.purpose: Validate the contribution of the learnable retriever through ablation studies against frozen retrievers and BM25 baselines across multiple tasks.

nodes.title: Capability: Dynamic Knowledge Updates
nodes.purpose: Provide evidence that replacing the non-parametric index (e.g., 2016 vs. 2018 Wikipedia) allows the model to update world knowledge without retraining parameters.

nodes.title: Limitations: Index Dependency and Collapse Risks
nodes.purpose: Acknowledge constraints such as reliance on the quality/bias of the external index (Wikipedia) and potential retrieval collapse on tasks with weak factual signals.

coverage_notes: The plan follows the paper's logical flow from problem definition to architecture, formalism, experimental validation across diverse tasks (QA, Generation, Classification), and finally analysis of mechanisms (retrieval learning, knowledge updating).
Nodes cover both the 'Sequence' and 'Token' variants which are central to the methodological contribution.
Experimental results are grouped by task type but linked back to the core argument of hybrid memory superiority.
